However, they also maintained distinctive local funerary traditions, such as burying their loved ones in rock-cut tombs, or artificial caves. Some of these caves contained external courtyards located in front of the burial chambers where animal offerings might have been made. Archaeologists even suspect that perishable foods or liquids were offered in characteristic island containers, such as high-bottomed vessels. Until now, however, the contents of these ceramic containers had never been identified.

stories.summary: University of Miami sophomore Scarlett Schremmer was disqualified after using an illegal green-reading book at Pelican Golf Club. Schremmer, who has won twice this fall competing for the Hurricanes, shot 69-74 to miss the cut prior to her disqualification. "Schremmer violated Model Local Rule G-11, which, per the LPGA Rules of Play Card, is in effect during all LPGA Tour competitions, except at off-site local qualifying events," the LPGA said in a statement. "This Model Local Rule requires that players are limited throughout their round to using only the yardage book that has been approved for use in the competition."
